title: Heartbeat
description:
Edge worker capacity heartbeat. Request body of POST /v1/capacity/heartbeat, and the shape GET /v1/status re-exposes verbatim for each edge placement.

AUTHORITY: edge/EDGE-WORKER-CONTRACT.md section 1 is the source of truth for these fields. This schema is a mechanical restatement of that table; where the two disagree, the edge contract wins and this file is the bug. Field semantics that the edge contract states in prose (R9, R11) are repeated in the descriptions below because an implementer reading only the schema must not be able to get them wrong.

A HEARTBEAT MAY NARROW STATIC AUTHORITY; IT MAY NEVER EXPAND IT.

    effective capability = Git/catalog authority INTERSECT runtime heartbeat observation

A heartbeat is an OBSERVATION submitted by the node itself. It can make a placement LESS eligible - the node is INTERACTIVE, the model is not loaded, free VRAM is below a floor - and the router acts on that immediately. It can NEVER grant a placement a model, a capability, a context size, or any other authority that the Git-managed catalog does not already give it. Specifically: active_model counts as warm ONLY when that model is catalog-authorized for that placement; a capability or max_context larger than the catalog's is capped at the catalog's; and a model, capability or context claim with no catalog counterpart is an observability/reconciliation ALARM and is IGNORED for eligibility rather than acted on.

Why this is written down here rather than left to the router: a self-report is not a model-authorization bypass - authorization is the per-model CEL policy and it does not read heartbeats - but an unconstrained self-report lets a compromised node BIAS PLACEMENT toward itself, which is a placement-integrity and potentially a confidentiality problem inside the approved edge trust boundary. Intersection is what keeps a stolen node credential to the blast radius of withdrawing its own capacity.

Dynamic measurements - gpu.vram_free_gb, gpu.utilization_pct, gpu.vram_total_gb, state - stay self-reported and may affect SCHEDULING. They never affect static authorization or capability membership.

PRESENCE: every field is required. Unlike the catalog (where an absent key and an explicit null mean the same thing), a heartbeat is generated by a known agent on a fixed schedule: a missing key means a broken agent, not an unknown value. Unmeasured values are sent explicitly as null, or as the literal string "unmeasured" where the edge contract says so.

node.description: Stable node identifier. Not necessarily the OS hostname, and deliberately not a network address. The bearer credential the node authenticates with is bound to this identifier: a heartbeat whose `node` does not match its credential is rejected 403 `node_identity_mismatch` rather than accepted for the wrong node.

state.description:
Self-reported state. STATE OWNERSHIP IS LOCAL: the host decides, the cluster never forces a node into SERVING.

AVAILABLE - idle, ready to accept work.
SERVING - actively handling one or more inference requests.
DRAINING - finishing in-flight requests, refusing new ones.
INTERACTIVE - local human use has claimed the GPU; not eligible for placement.
OFFLINE - the node reports it explicitly (e.g. a clean shutdown). The router ALSO assigns OFFLINE on its own when no heartbeat arrives inside 3x the interval; that transition is inferred from silence and never appears in a payload.

INTERACTIVE and DRAINING are withdrawal mechanism 1 of 3 (see README 'Withdrawal semantics'): agent-router marks the placement ineligible immediately, on receipt.

model.description: GPU model string. NOT nullable: the edge contract's field table types this as a string whose unmeasured encoding is the LITERAL STRING "unmeasured" (edge contract section 4, laptop), and null is reserved there for the two VRAM fields. A node with no hardware identity at all is out of contract and must be rejected rather than silently accepted. A router MUST NOT resolve an unmeasured model to a SKU by inference.

arch.description: GPU architecture, e.g. "gfx1100". NOT nullable, for the same reason as model: unmeasured is the literal string "unmeasured", per the edge contract's field table.

vram_total_gb.description: Total VRAM in GB. null means no measurement exists. A router MUST NOT satisfy a policy's min_vram_gb from a null value and MUST NOT substitute a nameplate figure for it (catalog README, 'Capacity numbers are sourced, not assumed').

vram_free_gb.description: Free VRAM in GB at sample time. null means no measurement exists. This is the only input to a policy's min_free_vram_gb; a null value cannot satisfy one.

utilization_pct.description: GPU utilization percentage at sample time. Not nullable, per the edge contract's field table. A node that cannot read utilization is out of contract; that tension is recorded in the README's open items rather than resolved by widening this type here.

kind.description: Runtime identifier, e.g. "llama-swap+llama.cpp". Informational: invariant 9 keeps runtime differences behind the OpenAI-compatible contract.

endpoint.description:
OBSERVATIONAL / STATUS METADATA ONLY (owner ruling R9). This field exists so an operator can see where a node believes it is listening. It MUST NOT become an authoritative routing target, MUST NOT cause dynamic agentgateway reconfiguration, and MUST NOT override Git-managed placement or backend topology. agentgateway backend hostnames stay Git-managed.

THREAT: a compromised edge heartbeat credential must not be able to redirect inference traffic by advertising an arbitrary endpoint. This is a security boundary, not a style preference. It pairs with R5 (x-placement is a scheduling signal, never authorization) as the two things a compromised edge or client cannot do.

Consequently /v1/place never returns an endpoint: a caller receives a placement NAME and reaches it through agentgateway, never a URL from this field. No format is asserted on this string because it is never dereferenced by the control plane; placeholder forms such as "https://<edge-host>:<edge-port>" are legal values in documents.

active_model.description:
OWNER RULING R11 - the model currently LOADED / WARM IN THE INFERENCE RUNTIME, i.e. servable now with no load step. null when nothing is loaded.

IDENTIFIER NAMESPACE (canonical - one rule, shared with cached_models): the value is a CATALOG `model_id`, i.e. a key in the catalog `models` table, which for local models is the gateway-facing alias - "qwen36-27b". It is NOT the catalog's `upstream_model_id` ("qwen3.6-27b"), which is the different string agentgateway sends to the upstream server; the catalog states plainly that the two must not be swapped. The router derives readiness by joining this value against the catalog, so a heartbeat reporting the upstream id makes a warm node look cold. A node whose runtime knows only its upstream id translates before it reports.

A value matching no catalog model_id, or a model_id the catalog does not place on this node, does NOT make the node warm: it is an alarm (see the narrowing rule in this schema's top-level description) and is ignored for eligibility.

Warm, cached and absent are three different costs, and /v1/place economics depend on telling them apart. Collapsing warm into cached loses the ability to prefer a node that can answer immediately; collapsing cached into absent loses the ability to prefer a node that can load in seconds over one that must download tens of gigabytes. A model listed here is normally also present in cached_models, but a router MUST NOT assume it.

cached_models.description:
OWNER RULING R11 - model artifacts ALREADY PRESENT ON LOCAL STORAGE and therefore loadable WITHOUT A DOWNLOAD, but potentially still requiring model/VRAM load time. This is the middle cost between active_model (warm, zero load) and a model that appears in neither list (absent, download required). Empty array is legal and means no artifacts are resident.

Same identifier namespace as active_model: catalog `model_id` values, never `upstream_model_id`. An entry with no catalog counterpart, or one the catalog does not place on this node, is an alarm and is ignored for eligibility - a node cannot make itself a candidate for a model the catalog never placed there by listing it here.

preemptible.description: True if local interactive use can evict AI work on this host. Invariant 8: interactive human use of an edge host always wins, immediately, unilaterally, and with no cluster round-trip.

interactive.description: True while a human is actively using the host. state=INTERACTIVE implies this is true; the converse does not hold - a host can report interactive=true while DRAINING in-flight work before it flips to INTERACTIVE.

ac_power.description: False disqualifies a laptop placement (edge contract section 4). A battery-powered host advertises nothing.

cluster_reachable.description: The node's own view of whether it can reach the cluster, at its last self-check. A heartbeat that arrives asserts reachability by construction, so false here means the node's own probe failed (or the heartbeat is a replay of a buffered sample); the router SHOULD treat the node as ineligible for placement until a heartbeat reports true.

last_heartbeat.description: RFC 3339 timestamp STAMPED BY THE EDGE HOST, not by the router. The router records its own receipt time separately; the two differing is a clock-skew signal, not an error.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities this node's current runtime provides. Same vocabulary as the catalog's models[].capabilities, so a heartbeat can be checked against a profile's guaranteed capability floor without translation. vision and audio are INPUT modalities.

NARROWING ONLY. This list can REMOVE a capability the catalog grants - the runtime came up without tool calling, so the node is not a candidate for work that needs it. It can never ADD one: a capability here that the catalog does not grant this placement is an alarm, and the effective set is the intersection of the two.

max_context.description:
Context window in tokens that this node currently serves. Checked against a profile's min_context guarantee.

NARROWING ONLY. A value BELOW the catalog's figure for the model on this placement is honoured - the runtime was started with a smaller window and the node is not a candidate for work that needs more. A value ABOVE it is capped at the catalog's and raised as an alarm; a node cannot buy itself larger work by claiming a bigger window.

allOf.description: state=INTERACTIVE means a human has claimed the GPU, so interactive must agree. The reverse is deliberately not constrained.
